title: Cavity-QED analysis of InAs quantum-dot single photon production
authors: W. W. Chow, S. Peana, D. I. Herman, K. Y. Lee, A. Cejan, C. Shang, G. Moody, J. E. Bowers, F. Jahnke
abstract: Cavity quantum electrodynamics is used to study the extent cavity enhancement affects single photon performance of an InAs quantum dot, in terms of emission rate, purity and indistinguishability at different temperatures. Parametric studies show a tradeoff between single photon production rate and purity, as well as between indistinguishability and purity. The results indicate the importance of quantum carrier-photon correlations that yield substantial corrections to mean-field treatments, especially at high light-matter coupling strength, where cavity enhancement is most effective.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes single-photon generation from InAs quantum dots coupled to optical cavities using Cavity-QED. It models the system dynamics by incorporating complex quantum carrier-photon correlations into the equations of motion. The key finding is that these correlations significantly modify performance metrics like purity and rate, revealing crucial trade-offs that must be accounted for beyond simple mean-field approximations.
main_problem: The study investigates how cavity enhancement affects the single photon performance (rate, purity, and indistinguishability) of an InAs quantum dot.
main_result: The analysis reveals fundamental trade-offs between single photon production rate and purity, emphasizing that quantum carrier-photon correlations provide substantial corrections beyond mean-field predictions, especially at high coupling strengths.
method: The authors use a theoretical framework based on the Heisenberg picture, deriving equations of motion for various correlation terms and employing a factorization scheme to separate mean-field and correlation contributions.
model_or_system: The system modeled is an InAs quantum dot coupled to an optical micro- or nanocavity, described by a Hamiltonian involving photon, electron, and hole operators. The analysis tracks the evolution of populations and polarizations.
key_observables: Single photon emission rate ($\gamma_c n_p$), purity ($g^{(2)}(0)$), indistinguishability ($\eta_{ind}$), and coherence time ($	au_{coh}$).
important_parameters: Light-matter coupling strength ($g$), cavity photon decay rate ($\gamma_c$), dephasing rate ($\gamma$), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: Initial parametric studies often neglect correlation terms for computational ease, and the analysis assumes steady-state values for solving correlation functions.
figures_summary: Figures compare $\gamma_c n_p$ and $g^{(2)}(0)$ vs. pump rate or cavity lifetime, illustrating the impact of correlation terms and temperature on single-photon metrics.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by deriving equations of motion, performing parametric studies comparing mean-field vs. correlated results, and analyzing the resulting trade-offs between key single-photon metrics.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the non-trivial quantum corrections (beyond mean-field) necessary for accurately predicting single-photon sources in solid-state quantum emitters, a core topic in cavity QED.
